rule: published artifacts stay byte-identical; corrections are appended
found_by: C-T51's unit warning, applied to my own headline test

entries.source_section_or_line: arm A, FIRST PASS ONLY -- caught and corrected before publication
entries.old_statement: arm A was implemented as a 200 ms BIN MERGE and produced C(1) = -0.1742 / -0.1934 / -0.0670, i.e. NEGATIVE order-flow autocorrelation
entries.corrected_statement: That negative sign was manufactured by my own code. A bin merge collapses same-side runs WITHIN a bin, so the next event in the same bin must be the opposite side -- alternation is forced mechanically, and at 200 ms most consecutive events share a bin. It is also not what C-T19 did: tools/ct35 line 150 reads `keep = np.diff(ots0) >= 200`, a 200 ms DEAD-TIME THINNING of the order series, not a bin merge. Arm A was rebuilt as thinning and C(1) came back positive (+0.1226 / +0.0949 / +0.1045). The bin-merge numbers are VOID and were never published. Recorded because the tell was a corpus contradiction: Bouchaud's C(l) is a long-memory POSITIVE object and a negative C(1) is incompatible with it, which is what prompted the check.

entries.old_statement: the fine balance was presented as a single identity test with both inputs calibrated
entries.corrected_statement: The two inputs were estimated under DIFFERENT EVENT DEFINITIONS. kappa-chi (C-T27) runs on the (ts_ms, side) order collapse; gamma (C-T19) runs on a 200 ms dead-time thinning of that same series, and the two were combined without either side saying so. A lag of 10 orders and a lag of 10 thinned events are different amounts of time, so the identity was tested across two clocks. MEASURED, one thing varied: the event definition alone moves gamma by +0.1275 / -0.0872 / -0.0826, i.e. +5.60 / -3.47 / -2.88 recovery sd. Repaired -- both sides on the order collapse -- the VERDICT SURVIVES: BTC and SOL still reject, ETH still does not, and no symbol's side flips.

entries.source_section_or_line: gamma_sd and the derived z values
entries.old_statement: gamma's precision was reported as sd 0.023-0.029 and the fine-balance z values (-2.51 / +1.66 / -3.15) were computed from it
entries.corrected_statement: That sd is a SAMPLING sd, taken from C-T28's recovery study, and it is not the dominant uncertainty. gamma is now measured to be unstable to TWO separate specification choices, each larger than the sampling sd: the FIT RANGE (this lane's own earlier finding; ct35 fits [5,200] while ct28 documents [10,1000]) and the EVENT DEFINITION (measured this round at 2.88-5.60 sd). A quoted sd that omits both understates the uncertainty in gamma by several fold, so the published z values are OVERCONFIDENT and should be read as direction-of-evidence, not as calibrated significance. This does not change which symbols reject -- the repaired test rejects the same two -- but it removes any claim to a calibrated p-value on the fine balance.

entries.old_statement: C-T19's gamma is quoted as 0.407 / 0.379 / 0.411 across several drivers
entries.corrected_statement: I could not reproduce it. On the same seven days, with the dead-time thinning read out of ct35 line 150, my fit gives 0.1996 / 0.4188 / 0.2120 debiased against a published 0.3810 / 0.3466 / 0.3736. At least one further specification difference remains unaccounted for -- the fit range is one candidate, since ct35 fits [5,200] while ct28 documents the real gamma as fitted on [10,1000], and no driver named C-T19 survives on disk to settle it. Stated as an OPEN REPRODUCTION FAILURE, not as a refutation: the controlled A-vs-B contrast in this round is internally valid because one thing was varied inside one code path, and it does not depend on either arm matching C-T19.
